text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government will provide 4,000 tonnes of seeds worth 300 million shillings to famine hit regions under the drought recovery programme.
- The government says it has put in place measures to protect local industries from unfair competition arising from transit goods illegally diverted into the domestic market.
- Five Ugandans suspected of belonging to the clandestine February 18 Resistance Army are sentenced to death by a court in western Kenya for robbery with violence.
- Touts for matatu mini-bus taxis attack three suspected pickpockets, burning one to death, beating another to death and serious injuring the third.
- A gang of burglars hit Mombasa and neighbouring coastal holiday towns, stealing cash and property worth millions of shillings.
- President Daniel arap Moi calls on Africans to act decisively to stop the disintegration of their cultures under the impact of Western influences.
- A massive 48,000 tonnes of food aid is expected to arrive in Mombasa within the next 10 days.
- Members of the European Union parliament voice strong support for President Moi's initiative to find a permanent solution to the Sudanese conflict.
- Air Gabon will soon start a cargo service to Eldoret International airport. ($1=55 Kenyan shillings)
